recent.title: PROCESS FOR MILLING A KITCHEN SINK

patents.source: USPTO Open Data Portal, granted patents since 2001, applicant phrase "mila", 2026-10-09

reading.body:
Mila's patent record as captured here shows six granted patents, but the five most recent titles are kitchen fixtures, not AI research, indicating the applicant search matched a different entity.

The institute profile describes a nonprofit AI research community of more than 1,400 researchers, founded in 1993, with programs for policy training, startup support, and a venture arm. That profile is consistent with an AI research organization, but the dataset lists no products or cases for Mila, so it offers no direct measure of AI capability.

The patent titles, including a process for milling a kitchen sink, an air filter, a bain marie, and a side sink, are unrelated to machine learning. The source note says the query used the applicant phrase "mila", which likely captured a different organization. These records provide no signal about compute, buildings, or power constraints for AI.

profile_text.body:
Mila, also called Mila - Quebec Artificial Intelligence Institute, is a nonprofit artificial intelligence research institute based in Montreal, Quebec, Canada, founded in 1993. According to its site, it brings together researchers from Université de Montréal, McGill University, Polytechnique Montréal and HEC Montréal, and describes itself as a community of more than 1,400 researchers specializing in machine learning. It also offers training, including a generative AI productivity course with a next cohort scheduled online on October 6 and 8, 2026, and runs a venture arm that invests in founders in deep tech, AI, and STEM.

The site highlights research output, including a generative cutout animation system that takes a skeletal animation and a text prompt and generates a 2.5D cutout rig, using an SDS loss with a LoRA prior, and QueStER, a method that generates keyword-based search specifications executed by BM25 and is trained with reinforcement learning. No AI products, MCP servers, or lawsuits are recorded for the company.
